new_symbol_range_suggestions.K_P_sat: positive and on the product concentration scale; values comparable to reachable P produce visible saturation of K_i adaptation, while much larger values make the revised law approach the parent over the observed trajectory

derivation_notes: The catalytic rate law is unchanged, but the K_i dynamics are re-derived from a finite-capacity product-exposure mechanism: as product accumulates, the drive to further lower K_i saturates rather than increasing proportionally without bound. This keeps the existing closed-vessel states and directly alters the scored target through the evolving competitive term P/K_i.
change_summary: The linear-in-P adaptation drive for K_i was replaced by a saturating product-dependent drive. This creates a sharper mid-trajectory curvature change in dP_dt versus P and a later plateau in competitive-inhibition strengthening under appreciable product accumulation.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The effective inhibition-scale dynamics obey first-order decay with a product-proportional driving term -k_Ki_decay*P*(K_i-K_i_min).
assumption_audit.mechanism: Product-induced strengthening of competitive inhibition often reflects finite-site conformational or crowding adaptation, so the drive for further reduction in K_i should itself saturate as product occupancy or exposure becomes high.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: When K_P_sat is much larger than product concentrations visited on the trajectory, P/(K_P_sat + P) is approximately P/K_P_sat, so after absorbing the constant factor 1/K_P_sat into k_Ki_decay the observed K_i dynamics reduce to the parent's effectively linear-in-P form over that range.

response_change.parent_relation: The target rate decreases with product through an instantaneous competitive factor P/K_i and a single delayed noncompetitive suppression load I_slow, so product inhibition enters as one smooth phase of slowing tied directly to P and one linear relaxation toward P.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same inhibited Michaelis structure but relax the assumption that the competitive product-inhibition strength adapts linearly with cumulative product exposure; instead make that adaptation saturate with product so the target shows an early strong curvature change that later plateaus in its sensitivity to further product accumulation.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with the same initial substrate and enzyme settings, the child predicts that dP_dt versus P can bend more sharply at intermediate product levels and then partially stabilize because competitive inhibition strengthening saturates, whereas the parent keeps progressively changing inhibition strength in a single exponential-like fashion.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when product rises to a scale comparable to the adaptation-driving range so that K_i has moved appreciably away from its initial value but not yet fully to K_i_min; if product stays very low or K_i remains near constant, the contrast is weak.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate product accumulation already reveals departure from a single-phase decline in competitive inhibition scale; in holdout, later-time higher-product segments extend this into a visible plateau of K_i evolution and corresponding dP_dt curvature change.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the saturation of the revised K_i adaptation law to be effectively absent over the observed product range, so the adaptation reduces to the current linear-in-P decay form.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: finite-capacity product-driven adaptation of competitive inhibition strength
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Product-induced strengthening of competitive inhibition often reflects finite-site conformational or crowding adaptation, so the drive for further reduction in K_i should itself saturate as product occupancy/exposure becomes high.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the shape of the product-to-K_i drive from unbounded linear growth to a finite-capacity saturating response, which in turn changes the trajectory-level curvature of the scored dP_dt mapping through K_i rather than merely rescaling an existing term.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Competitive inhibition-scale adaptation is driven proportionally by product at all product levels.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Competitive inhibition-scale adaptation is driven by product with finite-capacity saturation at high product burden.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: As K_P_sat becomes much larger than observed P, the saturating drive behaves approximately linearly in P over the sampled trajectory after absorbing the scale into k_Ki_decay.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: With fixed initial substrate and enzyme settings, plotting dP_dt against P along the trajectory shows stronger intermediate bending followed by partial stabilization once product reaches the adaptation-driving range, because K_i evolution slows despite further product accumulation; the parent instead maintains a single-phase increase in adaptation drive proportional to P.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both an initially strong adaptation response and a later saturation of that same adaptation drive when both regimes are visible on one observed trajectory, because its K_i dynamics remain proportional to P throughout. Refitting V_max, K_m, K_icat, k_Ki_decay, or k_Islow_relax can shift rate scale or timing but cannot create the finite-capacity plateau in product-driven K_i evolution that directly feeds back into the scored dP_dt mapping.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when product rises to a scale comparable to the adaptation-driving range so that K_i has moved appreciably away from its initial value but not yet fully to K_i_min; if product stays very low or K_i remains near constant, the contrast is weak.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate product accumulation already reveals departure from a single-phase decline in competitive inhibition scale; in holdout, later-time higher-product segments extend this into a visible plateau of K_i evolution and corresponding dP_dt curvature change.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the saturation of the revised K_i adaptation law to be effectively absent over the observed product range, so the adaptation reduces to the current linear-in-P decay form.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The model assumes the product-driven evolution of the effective competitive inhibition constant is proportional to P at all product levels, implying unlimited growth in adaptation drive as product accumulates before the asymptote is reached.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The effective inhibition-scale dynamics obey first-order decay with a product-proportional driving term -k_Ki_decay*P*(K_i-K_i_min).
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Product-induced strengthening of competitive inhibition often reflects finite-site conformational or crowding adaptation, so the drive for further reduction in K_i should itself saturate as product occupancy/exposure becomes high.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the linear exposure assumption in the K_i state equation, not to add a wholly new process. The parent target mapping has a single-phase shortcut: for fixed V_max, K_m, K_icat, and k_Islow_relax, the scored rate changes with product through one instantaneous competitive term and one delayed suppression state, while the competitive-adaptation state K_i is driven by a linearly increasing function of P. Varying time along the standard closed-vessel trajectory changes P while initial conditions and enzyme conditions are held fixed. Under admissible conditions where product reaches moderate to high levels and K_i is still above K_i_min, the child would show a different dP_dt-versus-P curvature: early product rise can strengthen inhibition noticeably, but later increases in P produce diminishing additional change in K_i and therefore a partial flattening of the rate-law distortion. A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both an initially strong adaptation response and a later saturation of that same adaptation drive if both are visible on the same observed trajectory, because its K_i dynamics remain proportional to P throughout. This affects the target mapping directly, not only an auxiliary state, since K_i enters the denominator of dP_dt. The contrast is limited when P never leaves the low-product regime or when K_i is already near K_i_min, in which case the refinement may be practically unidentifiable.

scenario_text: A soluble enzyme converts a finite substrate pool into product in a closed biochemical reaction vessel. Substrate depletion and product accumulation are tracked jointly from specified initial amounts, while enzyme activity and solution conditions remain fixed. The target is the instantaneous product-formation rate along the reaction trajectory.
